claim: scripts/ml/fc_geometry_resolve.py:_join_real_r() joins the 'real' realized-R arm of the fc-geometry live-vs-counterfactual comparison to the closed trades table by (symbol, nearest timestamp within 900s) only -- it never filters on trades.strategy_name (or account_id), although the soak row it resolves for carries both fields and config/strategies.yaml runs 9 distinct strategies on BTCUSDT alone that can each close a trade inside that same 900s window, so the 'real arm' can be silently attributed to the WRONG strategy's trade.
evidence: PYTHONPATH=. python3 docs/audits/code-audit-2026-09-27/CA-B02-repros/fc_geom_join.py.txt -> 'joined real_r = -3.0 (picked the CLOSEST-in-time trade regardless of strategy)' / 'this soak row belongs to trend_donchian (true R=2.0) but the join has no strategy filter and returns the nearer ict_scalp_5m trade's R instead: -3.0' -- a synthetic sqlite trades table with a trend_donchian close (true R=+2.0, 5 min after decision time) and an unrelated ict_scalp_5m close (R=-3.0, 3 min after decision time) returns the WRONG strategy's R because it is merely closer in time. python3 -c "import yaml; d=yaml.safe_load(open('config/strategies.yaml')); print([k for k,v in (d.get('strategies',d)).items() if isinstance(v,dict) and 'BTCUSDT' in (v.get('symbols') or v.get('symbol') or [])])" -> ['turtle_soup', 'trend_donchian', 'fade_breakout_4h', 'squeeze_breakout_4h', 'vwap', 'ict_scalp_5m', 'fvg_range_15m', 'htf_pullback_trend_2h', 'trend_donchian_1h'] (9 strategies share BTCUSDT).
location: scripts/ml/fc_geometry_resolve.py:119-147 (_join_real_r, the SQL at :125-129 selects only WHERE symbol=? AND status='closed' AND is_backtest=0 -- no strategy_name predicate), called at :214
expected: The realized R attributed to a soak row should belong to the SAME strategy/leg the soak row itself records (r.get('strategy'), r.get('account_id')).
actual: The join picks whichever closed trade on that symbol is nearest in time, regardless of strategy or account, whenever more than one strategy trades the same symbol.
population: 9 of the ~N live BTCUSDT-trading strategies measured against config/strategies.yaml on main; every fc-geometry soak row for any of those 9 strategies is exposed to the same mis-join whenever another one of the 9 also closed a BTCUSDT trade within 900s of it. No test file exists for scripts/ml/fc_geometry_resolve.py (verified by grep across tests/).
blast_radius: money-at-risk (this script produces the evidence for a live SL/TP-geometry design decision, MB-20260705-FC-SLTP-GEOMETRY; a corrupted real-vs-counterfactual comparison can wrongly justify or reject a live geometry change)
detector: PI-20260927-CAB02-0002 (docs/claude/work/pipeline/); no existing test covers this file -- proposed: a regression test with two concurrent same-symbol, different-strategy closes asserting _join_real_r picks the matching strategy's row.
proposed_fix: Thread strategy (and ideally account_id) from the soak row into _join_real_r() and add 'AND strategy_name=?' to the SQL; add the missing test.

claim: scripts/ml/m23_ev_gate.py sweeps ~50 decision thresholds over the SAME held-out cohort it then reports net-R/win-rate for, and picks the threshold that maximizes net R on that same set (`if best is None or net_r > best[0]`) -- an in-sample multiple-comparisons selection that systematically overstates the apparent edge of the selected threshold. This is the identical selection-bias shape CA-B01 already flagged (as low, 0 adopted manifests) in scripts/ml/hpo_sweep.py; here it is used to produce the 'SELECTION EV POSITIVE/NOT POSITIVE' verdict that multiple committed research memos (docs/research/M23-phase1-*, M23-phase2-*) cite directly as GO/NO-GO evidence on real model-promotion candidates (e.g. 'M23 meta-labeling -- NO-GO on P3', docs/sprint-logs/S-ROADMAP-STATUS-REVIEW-2026-08-01.md).
evidence: PYTHONPATH=. python3 docs/audits/code-audit-2026-09-27/CA-B02-repros/m23_selection_bias.py.txt -> 'picked-in-sample: t*=0.9905 n_sel=2 net_r=-1.16 beats_takeall=True usable=False' on a scorer with prob assigned by random.random() (zero predictive skill by construction, independent of R) -- 'beats_takeall=True' despite zero real skill. PYTHONPATH=. python3 docs/audits/code-audit-2026-09-27/CA-B02-repros/m23_selection_bias_montecarlo.py.txt -> 'of 300 pure-noise trials (n=400 rows each, real base rate 0.244, cost 0.05R): 300/300 beats take-all by the in-sample-max threshold, 3/300 cross BOTH beats-takeall AND the usable-volume floor despite the scorer carrying zero real predictive skill by construction' -- i.e. the 'beats take-all' check alone is satisfied ~100% of the time by pure chance, and even the volume-floor-gated 'usable POSITIVE' verdict has a measured ~1% false-positive rate under zero skill.
location: scripts/ml/m23_ev_gate.py:152-186 (threshold sweep + `best` selection over the same `scored` cohort used for the reported metrics)
expected: A verdict used as GO/NO-GO evidence for a real-money model promotion candidate should not have a quantifiable false-positive rate purely from evaluating many thresholds on one dataset with no held-out validation split for the threshold choice itself.
actual: best-threshold selection and its reported performance come from the same rows, with no nested/held-out split; ~1% of zero-skill scorers still cross both the beats-takeall and usable-volume bars by chance alone.
population: scripts/ml/m23_ev_gate.py (193 lines), the only file implementing this gate; cited by 6 committed docs/research/M23-*.md memos and 1 sprint-log status review as the GO/NO-GO source for the setup-candidates-metalabel-backtest-v1 family. No test file exists for this script (verified by grep across tests/). All verdicts observed in committed docs to date read 'below usable-volume floor / NOT (yet)' (i.e. the currently-observed direction is conservative, not a live false-positive) -- this finding is about the method's bias, not a claim that today's specific verdict is wrong.
blast_radius: money-at-risk (indirect -- feeds promotion-candidate GO/NO-GO research decisions, not yet a live order path)
detector: no existing test or CI guard checks this gate's selection-bias property; proposed: a nested-CV or held-out-threshold-selection variant, or at minimum a printed caveat + a synthetic zero-skill self-test analogous to evidence_floor_report.py's --self-test.
proposed_fix: Split the live holdout cohort itself into a threshold-selection slice and a reporting slice (or use nested nested-CV), and print the selection-bias caveat next to the verdict the way m23_ev_gate.py already prints the r_multiple_source fallback caveat.
disposition: verified-non-issue-in-current-observed-direction / filed-as-methodology (not added to pipeline -- see CA-B02.md rationale; low urgency because 0 GO verdicts produced to date, same class as the already-filed hpo_sweep low finding from CA-B01)
